title: Boss: Event Log Tools
summary: Closures, this, higher-order functions and immutable updates together.

steps.title: The job
steps.body: You are building small utilities for an app's event log. Each one is a function that returns a function or an object with private state, and none may mutate what it is given.

steps.title: Rate limiter
steps.prompt: Write `limit(max: number, fn: (msg: string) => void)` returning a function that calls `fn` for the first `max` messages and ignores the rest, returning `true` when it called `fn` and `false` when it dropped the message.
starter: function limit(max: number, fn: (msg: string) => void): (msg: string) => boolean {
solution: function limit(max: number, fn: (msg: string) => void): (msg: string) => boolean {

steps.title: Event store
prompt: Write `createLog()` returning `{ add(type, data), events(), byType(type) }`:
- `add` appends `{ seq, type, data }` where `seq` counts up from 1
- `events()` returns a **copy** of all events (changing it must not affect the log)
- `byType(type)` returns the events of that type
`add` must work when passed around as a callback (`["x", "y"].forEach(t => log.add(t, null))` and also `const add = log.add; add("z", 1)`).
starter: type LogEvent = { seq: number; type: string; data: unknown };
solution: type LogEvent = { seq: number; type: string; data: unknown };
template: Dojo.eq("events()", [{ seq: 1, type: "login", data: { user: "ada" } }, { seq: 2, type: "click", data: 1 }, { seq: 3, type: "login", data: { user: "bo" } }], dojoLog.events());
hints: Use arrow functions for the three members so a detached `add` still works (they use the closure, not `this`).

steps.title: Pipeline of transforms
prompt: Write `pipeline(...steps)` where each step is `(events: LogEvent[]) => LogEvent[]`, returning one function that runs them left to right.
`pipeline(only("login"), lastN(1))(events)` returns the most recent login event.
starter: type LogEvent = { seq: number; type: string; data: unknown };
solution: type LogEvent = { seq: number; type: string; data: unknown };
return events => steps.reduce((acc, step) => step(acc), events);
template: Dojo.eq("only login then last 1", [{ seq: 3, type: "login", data: "bo" }], pipeline(only("login"), lastN(1))(dojoE));
Dojo.eq("last 3 then only click", [2, 4], pipeline(lastN(3), only("click"))(dojoE).map(e => e.seq));
